newsitem.title: USA: Chinese defense minister to visit United States.
newsitem.headline: Chinese defense minister to visit United States.

text.p: In a sign of improving relations between Washington and Beijing, the Pentagon announced on Monday that Chinese Defense Minister Chi Haotian will visit the United States for two weeks beginning Dec. 5.

The statement said Chi and a 20-member senior delegation from the Chinese defense and foreign ministries will hold talks with Defense Secretary William Perry and other senior U.S. officials. Perry visited China in October 1994.

Chi had been scheduled to visit Washington last March but the United States called off the visit because of high tension between the two powers over what Washington called Chinese military pressure to influence elections in Taiwan.

The Clinton administration and Chinese leaders have moved to improve ties in recent weeks, including a visit to China by Secretary of State Warren Christopher and talks between Clinton and Chinese President Jiang Zemin on Sunday at a meeting of Asia-Pacific leaders in the Philippines.

"The objectives of this (Chi) visit are to exchange views on global and Asia-Pacific regional security issues of mutual concern and to discuss future prospects for bilateral military relations," the Pentagon statement said.

Despite U.S. concern over human rights in China, trade matters and reports that China may have provided nuclear technology to Pakistan and Iran, the Pentagon said Chi would travel to several U.S. military bases.
He will wind up his trip with talks at the U.S. Pacific Command in Hawaii Dec. 16-18.
